items.definition:
to deny any responsibility or support for
The politician was quick to disavow the controversial statements.

to make someone feel bitter or resentful
His constant failures began to embitter him.

teach (a person or group) to accept a set of beliefs uncritically
The cult tried to indoctrinate new members with its ideology.

to forbid or prohibit
The law proscribes the use of certain chemicals in food production.

to prove (a statement or charge) to be false
The lawyer tried to rebut the witness's testimony.

to free from a burden or impediment
He sought to unencumber himself from all his worldly possessions.

criticize unfairly; disparage
It's wrong to denigrate someone's efforts without understanding their challenges.

free (someone or something) from a difficulty or constraint
It took a long time to extricate the car from the mud.

to change the form of a word to express a grammatical function
Verbs in English do not inflect as much as in other languages.

be the strongest or main element; be greater in number or amount
In the forest, oak trees tend to predominate over other species.

to arrange in a series or sequence
The software needs to serialize the data before saving it.

to agree to a demand, request, or treaty
The government was forced to accede to the protesters' demands.

talk in a loud, aggressive, or arrogant way
He tried to bluster his way out of trouble.

To make something illegal.
Many countries have chosen to criminalize certain drugs.

make or seek to make an excessive or unfair profit
Some companies were accused of trying to profiteer during the crisis.

satisfy (a desire or an appetite) to the full
A good meal will sate your hunger.

to envy someone the possession or enjoyment of something
I don't begrudge him his success.

deliberately avoid using; abstain from
He tried to eschew all forms of luxury.

to treat (a person or animal) with a vaccine to produce immunity against a disease
Doctors inoculate children against various diseases.

spread through or over
A warm glow began to suffuse the room as the sun set.

to cause (a machine or device) to operate
The sensor actuates the alarm when motion is detected.

to confuse or muddle (someone's mind)
The complex instructions began to addle his brain.

to make (something bad or unsatisfactory) better
Steps were taken to ameliorate the living conditions of the refugees.

Puzzle, confuse, or bewilder.
The complex instructions left him completely bemused.

Polish (something, especially metal) by rubbing.
He used a soft cloth to burnish the silver.

Remove from a position of power or authority.
The challenger hoped to dethrone the reigning champion.

To preserve a body from decay
Ancient Egyptians would embalm their pharaohs.

To make (guilt or an offense) seem less serious or more forgivable
There were no circumstances to extenuate his actions.

to complain or cry fretfully
The baby started to grizzle when he couldn't reach his toy.

To dispense or allot justice, punishment, or harsh treatment.
The judge will mete out justice to the criminals.

To interpret (something, especially a person's words or actions) wrongly.
Don't misconstrue my silence as disapproval.

to decide or determine beforehand; to destine
Some believe that our destiny is preordained by a higher power.

to charm or enchant someone, sometimes in a deceptive way
She was beguiled by his charming smile.

to analyze or break down (a text or concept) into its component parts
The literary critic sought to deconstruct the novel's themes.

to utter suddenly; to expel semen
He would often ejaculate a witty remark during the meeting.

to shock or excite (someone) into taking action; to coat (iron or steel) with a protective layer of zinc
The urgency of the situation helped to galvanise the team into action.
